title: Air India Cuts Nearly 100 Flights as Iran War Sends Costs Soaring
excerpt: Tata-owned carrier reduces international capacity by 20% through July, delays staff pay hikes as jet fuel prices spike on Hormuz disruptions
body:
Air India is slashing nearly 100 international flights through July 2026 as the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran drives jet fuel prices to multi-year highs and forces airlines worldwide into emergency cost-cutting mode.

CEO Campbell Wilson confirmed the cuts in a staff memo last week, citing unprofitable long-haul routes and soaring operating costs. The airline, which Tata Group acquired in 2022 for a symbolic rupee, now faces projected annual losses of $600 million — roughly double what the conglomerate had budgeted for its turnaround plan.

**The Fuel Squeeze:** The Strait of Hormuz disruptions have pushed Brent crude past $104 a barrel, with aviation turbine fuel in India up nearly 30% since January. Pakistani airspace closures — a consequence of the wider regional conflict — have forced carriers to reroute flights between India and Europe, adding 90 minutes and thousands of dollars in fuel costs to each journey. Indian airlines collectively have absorbed over 500 crore rupees in losses from cancellations and rerouting since March.

**What Is Being Cut:** Air India is trimming frequencies on routes to London, New York, San Francisco, and several Gulf destinations — precisely the corridors most used by the Indian diaspora. Some routes will see three weekly flights reduced to two; others will shift to smaller aircraft. The airline has also delayed annual salary increases by a quarter, though it has ruled out layoffs for now.

**The Wider Aviation Fallout:** Air India is not alone. Emirates, Turkish Airlines, and Lufthansa have collectively cancelled over 12,000 flights globally in 2026. IndiGo, India's largest carrier, has also trimmed Gulf routes. Average international airfares are up 16% year-on-year, according to industry data, with summer travel bookings showing passengers booking earlier to lock in prices.

For the 4.4 million Indian-Americans and millions of NRIs worldwide, the cuts land hardest on the routes that connect them to family. Peak summer travel season — when diaspora families traditionally fly home for weddings, festivals, and school breaks — now comes with fewer seats, higher fares, and longer itineraries. Travelers on the India-US corridor should expect schedule changes on Air India's flagship Newark, JFK, and San Francisco routes through at least mid-July.

**What to Watch:** Whether Tata Group injects fresh capital into Air India's turnaround, and whether the government intervenes with aviation fuel tax relief as the conflict drags on.
nri_angle: Flight cuts on India-US and India-UK corridors directly impact millions of NRIs during peak summer travel season, with fewer seats and higher fares on the routes that connect them to family.
author: Diaspora Desk
